chunks: And inscribe for us good in this world and in the Hereafter; indeed, we have turned to You.
He said: My punishment strikes whom I will, but My mercy encompasses all things. So I will write it for those who take heed, who pay the zakat, and who believe in Our signs.

key_terms.آيَاتِنَا: Our signs, verses of the Quran
key_terms.الْآخِرَةِ: the Hereafter, the life to come

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for receiving God's specific mercy and good in this world and the Hereafter according to Surah Al-A'raf?
ai.summary: This passage, often cited in Shia supplications such as those in Sahifa Sajjadiyya, highlights the dialectic between divine justice and mercy, affirming that while punishment is selective, mercy is universal yet specifically realized through taqwa and charity. It underscores the Shia emphasis on the interplay between faith (iman), righteous action (amal), and divine grace, positioning the pious as the primary recipients of God's all-encompassing rahmah.
